title: Acme Retail POC — load & cost evaluation (Mar 2026)
content:
Executive summary:

This document captures the load-testing and cost evaluation we ran for the Acme Retail POC (product search + assistant scenarios). Goal: show three deployment options (hosted API, Redwood Dedicated, Redwood Private) at realistic traffic patterns and provide recommended configuration to meet Acme's SLOs (p95 latency <= 220ms for conversational queries, >= 200 qps for search embeddings pipeline) while minimizing unit cost.

Key takeaways:
- Hosted API (redwood-open-7b, standard instance routing) met p95 latency for low concurrency (<= 50 concurrent users) but degraded above ~150 concurrent active sessions; tail latencies spiked due to preemption and multi-tenant batching variability. Cost estimate: $1,050 — $1,400 per 1M tokens depending on burst usage patterns.
- Dedicated (2x A100-80GB pool, model pinned to redwood-open-7b-quant) delivered consistent p95 ~ 110–130ms at sustained 250 qps for chat generation and stable KV cache hit rates. Unit cost estimate: ~$620 per 1M tokens (after reserved commitment discounts).
- Private (on-prem test cluster w/ H100 equivalents) showed best latency at high concurrency but required additional infra ops and had a higher fixed cost; effective unit cost depends on utilization — favorable only at >70% sustained utilization for 6+ months.

Test scope and scenarios:
- Two primary workload patterns: (1) Conversational assistant (avg prompt tokens 60, response tokens 80, 1–3 tool calls possible) and (2) Search/embedding pipeline (query embeddings single call, batched 8–32 queries).
- Traffic profiles: baseline (50 active users), target (250 concurrent users), burst (1000 concurrent users for 10m).
- Models tested: redwood-open-7b (fp16), redwood-open-7b-quantized-INT8 (dedicated/private), redwood-open-13b (baseline for quality checks).
- Hardware variants: shared-hosted routing (mixed GPUs), Dedicated A100-80GB x2 & x4, Private H100-equivalent single-node and 4-node clusters.

Methodology:
- Load harness: redwood-loadbench v0.9 (internal), scripted to replay representative conversation traces from Acme's anonymized dataset (sample size 1.2k sessions).
- Latency metrics: p50, p90, p95, p99 measured at token-level and request-level. Throughput measured in qps and tokens/s. Cost estimated from token accounting + infra cost (reserved vs burst pricing) + operational overhead (SRE).
- Warm-up: each run includes a 20m warm-up to prime KV caches; cache-hit rate measured separately. Each steady-state run lasted 30m and results are averaged across three runs.
- Prompts included tool calls simulation (2% of requests) to emulate small external latency variance.

Raw (representative) results summary:
- Hosted API (model: redwood-open-7b, config: default routing, concurrency per instance auto):
  * Baseline (50 conc): p50=70ms, p95=180ms, qps sustained=90, tokens/s=14k, cost est=~$1,050/1M tokens
  * Target (250 conc): p50=220ms, p95=420ms (tail spikes), qps=210 sustained, observed 8% error rate under burst fallback during 2/3rd run
  * Burst (1000 conc): p95 > 2s, many requests dropped/fallback to CPU path; not acceptable for production SLA

- Dedicated (2x A100-80GB, pinned redwood-open-7b-quantized-INT8, batching tuned):
  * Baseline (50 conc): p50=45ms, p95=92ms, qps=180, tokens/s=28k, cache-hit ~ 24% (prefix reuse)
  * Target (250 conc): p50=110ms, p95=130ms, qps=540 sustained (queueing within batcher), tokens/s=85k, errors<0.5%
  * Burst (1000 conc, 4x pool): p95=170ms, qps=2.1k, tokens/s=330k, infra usage 92%
  * Cost est (after reserved commitments): ~$620/1M tokens; if spot-like burst capacity used, peak cost increases to ~$810/1M

- Private on-prem (H100-equivalent single node):
  * Baseline (50 conc): p50=30ms, p95=65ms, qps=240, tokens/s=36k
  * Target (250 conc): single-node saturated: p95=210ms with queueing; 4-node cluster: p95=95–120ms, qps=1.05k, tokens/s=165k
  * Fixed monthly infra amortized estimate: adds ~$46k/mo to cost base; unit cost favorable only at high utilization (>70% sustained)

Quality considerations (short sample eval):
- redwood-open-7b-quantized produced indistinguishable output for core product search and short assistant prompts in 92% of automated eval checks. 13b remains better for long-form creative responses; consider hybrid routing by intent.

Observability / failure modes observed:
- Hosted: multi-tenant preemption and background maintenance windows caused sudden latency spikes. Observability gaps: lacked token-granular traces for model internal scheduling — recommended instrumentation.
- Dedicated: batch queue saturation if per-request variance > 300 tokens; improved by dynamic max-batch-size and small per-tenant soft limits.
- Private: network egress to tool integrations can dominate tail latency; colocate critical tool endpoints where possible.

Recommendations for Acme Retail POC:
1) Short term (POC / narrow rollout): Use Dedicated with 2x A100-80GB, pinned quantized 7b model. Rationale: consistent latency under target concurrency, clear cost advantage vs hosted for sustained traffic, faster time-to-value than full private deployment.
2) Production rollout (6–18 months): Start with Dedicated + autoscale burst pool (allow hosted fallback for extra peaks). Implement intent-based routing: lightweight queries to quantized 7b, long-form to 13b on lower-throughput pool.
3) Private only if Acme commits to high utilization or regulatory needs requiring on-prem. If pursued, recommend a 4-node H100-equivalent cluster with on-site ops support and a 12–18 month utilization plan.
4) Monitoring & SLOs: p95 latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate, and cost-per-token. Add token-level traces for any production-hosted routes.

Proposed configuration (immediate POC):
- Model: redwood-open-7b-quantized-INT8 (pinned)
- Dedicated pool: 2x A100-80GB (initial), horizontal autoscale to 4x for bursts, reserved capacity commit: 6 months
- Batching config: dynamic batching enabled with target latency 100ms, max-batch-size=512, batch-timeout=12ms (tuned during runs)
- Cache: prefix-KV enabled; warm-up script to prepopulate top-5k queries per hour
- Fallback policy: health-check to hosted API for overflow with graceful degrade (truncate responses to maintain latency)

Open questions / Risks:
- Quality regressions for longer responses when routing to 7b quantized — request detailed eval from product for top N failure cases (Marcus).
- Bursting economics: need to finalize committed discount terms to validate $620/1M token estimate (Sales/Finance).
- Integrations: some tool calls (external search) add 50–250ms; need to measure end-to-end with real customer endpoints.

Next steps and action items:
- [Priya] Deliver this report to ACME technical stakeholders and schedule walkthrough week of Mar 15 (owner: Priya)
- [Diego] Attach automated eval artifacts (diffs for 100 sample prompts) to Confluence page (due Mar 12)
